text.p: Tropical Cyclone Gretelle, with 75 mph winds, is in the southern Mozambique Channel near 26s/35e, drifting west southwest. Gretelle is expected to continue this motion, slowly but steadily weakening during the next 24 hours. During this time, it will be close enough to the northeast coast of South Africa to spread rain squalls into the region. Shipping will be threatened. Heavy surf may lead to some flooding along the coast of eastern South Africa and southeastern Mozambique.
Tropical Cyclone Freda, in the southern Pacific near 27s/177e, has 55 mph winds but is weakening rapidly. It is expected to drift southeastward and dissipate by 48 hours. Only shipping is threatened.
Tropical Cyclone Pancho-Helinda will threaten shipping over the open Indian Ocean. The storm has 55 mph top winds and is near 10s/94e, moving east at 4 mph. It may intensify further.
There are no further statements at this time.
